drug_drug_interactions.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant and antiplatelet inhibition, coupled with direct gastric mucosal erosion. Extreme risk of major gastrointestinal and intracranial hemorrhage.
NSAIDs inhibit platelet cyclooxygenase and can displace warfarin from albumin binding sites, prolonging prothrombin time and causing gastric hemorrhage.
ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone production, impairing renal potassium excretion. Co-administration increases danger of lethal cardiac dysrhythmias.
Omeprazole inhibits hepatic CYP2C19, blocking the bio-activation of clopidogrel and increasing the risk of recurrent thrombotic events.
Iodinated intravascular radiocontrast media can induce acute renal failure, precipitating toxic accumulation of metformin and severe lactic acidosis.
Ciprofloxacin potently inhibits hepatic CYP1A2, drastically reducing theophylline clearance and causing refractory seizures and ventricular tachycardia.
Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4-mediated metabolism of simvastatin, elevating statin blood levels and increasing risk of severe myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
Concomitant use of ACE inhibitor and ARB does not confer additional benefit and substantially elevates risk of syncope, hyperkalemia, and acute renal failure.
